config._doc: vLLM half of the 2026-08-30 concurrency run (run-request-2026-08-30-n1248.md). Keys are (host, backend, label). max_model_len is 2048, not 8192: the ramp prompt plus its 475-token budget never exceeds ~490 tokens, and a larger window only reserves KV that is never touched -- at 8192 the KV cache alone is 9.66 GB for Qwen3-4B (8 KV heads, no GQA compression) and 12.88 GB for the 14B, which puts both off their cards for reasons that have nothing to do with the model. max_num_seqs is 8 because the concurrency grid tops out at n=8; a smaller value would cap the ramp and produce a false plateau. Split per host so each run's `hosts` matches its entries exactly (run.py:254 DE-11 refuses an entry pinned to an unsurveyed host); the two halves run concurrently on separate machines.

identity_refusals.concurrency: `max_num_seqs` — the scheduler's batch width, which is what this field means — is not on vLLM 0.26.0's HTTP surface. Searched exhaustively on 2026-08-18: every parameterless GET in the server's own /openapi.json route table (11 answered) on srv1 and srv2, including /server_info's full engine config, all 122 /metrics series, and /v1/models. `vllm:cache_config_info.kv_cache_max_concurrency` looks like the answer and is NOT: it is KV-cache capacity, and it moves opposite to the flag — srv1 ran --max-num-seqs 8 and reported 16.004, srv2 ran 16 and reported 5.314. It is not unknowable, only unaskable: a concurrency ramp recovers it, and on srv1 it read the knee at exactly 8 — throughput plateauing at 106.5 tok/s and per-request latency flat at ~9.5s through n=8 before the queue forms. That is a measurement this capture must not make, because it would perturb the run it describes. The raw metrics are under native

weights.method: sha256 over every tensor's bytes in sorted key order across all shards, computed on the serving host: this engine states no weights digest on any endpoint

serving_config.note: two digests because one would move when somebody enabled a counter; the semantic half is the one a guard could key on. Nothing reads either for comparison (ADR-0027 D7)

readings.note: both plateaus are reported because their disagreement is readable: on a wide server they differ by design, since a larger batch is slower per request before any queueing starts. NEITHER is a slot count: an engine configured one slot returned a throughput plateau several times that. Computed on the levels that fully succeeded — see levels_used and levels_dropped. The former `batches` boolean is retired (D1): it claimed to say which column to believe, and the two columns measure different things

concurrency.method: aggregate throughput against offered concurrency. The lowest level reaching PLATEAU_FRACTION of peak is the SATURATION POINT, which is a property of this host under this load — not a slot count, and not comparable across token budgets

identity_refusals.concurrency: `max_num_seqs` — the scheduler's batch width, which is what this field means — is not on vLLM 0.26.0's HTTP surface. Searched exhaustively on 2026-08-18: every parameterless GET in the server's own /openapi.json route table (11 answered) on srv1 and srv2, including /server_info's full engine config, all 122 /metrics series, and /v1/models. `vllm:cache_config_info.kv_cache_max_concurrency` looks like the answer and is NOT: it is KV-cache capacity, and it moves opposite to the flag — srv1 ran --max-num-seqs 8 and reported 16.004, srv2 ran 16 and reported 5.314. It is not unknowable, only unaskable: a concurrency ramp recovers it, and on srv1 it read the knee at exactly 8 — throughput plateauing at 106.5 tok/s and per-request latency flat at ~9.5s through n=8 before the queue forms. That is a measurement this capture must not make, because it would perturb the run it describes. The raw metrics are under native

weights.method: sha256 over every tensor's bytes in sorted key order across all shards, computed on the serving host: this engine states no weights digest on any endpoint

serving_config.note: two digests because one would move when somebody enabled a counter; the semantic half is the one a guard could key on. Nothing reads either for comparison (ADR-0027 D7)

readings.note: both plateaus are reported because their disagreement is readable: on a wide server they differ by design, since a larger batch is slower per request before any queueing starts. NEITHER is a slot count: an engine configured one slot returned a throughput plateau several times that. Computed on the levels that fully succeeded — see levels_used and levels_dropped. The former `batches` boolean is retired (D1): it claimed to say which column to believe, and the two columns measure different things

concurrency.method: aggregate throughput against offered concurrency. The lowest level reaching PLATEAU_FRACTION of peak is the SATURATION POINT, which is a property of this host under this load — not a slot count, and not comparable across token budgets

identity_refusals.concurrency: `max_num_seqs` — the scheduler's batch width, which is what this field means — is not on vLLM 0.26.0's HTTP surface. Searched exhaustively on 2026-08-18: every parameterless GET in the server's own /openapi.json route table (11 answered) on srv1 and srv2, including /server_info's full engine config, all 122 /metrics series, and /v1/models. `vllm:cache_config_info.kv_cache_max_concurrency` looks like the answer and is NOT: it is KV-cache capacity, and it moves opposite to the flag — srv1 ran --max-num-seqs 8 and reported 16.004, srv2 ran 16 and reported 5.314. It is not unknowable, only unaskable: a concurrency ramp recovers it, and on srv1 it read the knee at exactly 8 — throughput plateauing at 106.5 tok/s and per-request latency flat at ~9.5s through n=8 before the queue forms. That is a measurement this capture must not make, because it would perturb the run it describes. The raw metrics are under native

weights.method: sha256 over every tensor's bytes in sorted key order across all shards, computed on the serving host: this engine states no weights digest on any endpoint

serving_config.note: two digests because one would move when somebody enabled a counter; the semantic half is the one a guard could key on. Nothing reads either for comparison (ADR-0027 D7)

readings.note: both plateaus are reported because their disagreement is readable: on a wide server they differ by design, since a larger batch is slower per request before any queueing starts. NEITHER is a slot count: an engine configured one slot returned a throughput plateau several times that. Computed on the levels that fully succeeded — see levels_used and levels_dropped. The former `batches` boolean is retired (D1): it claimed to say which column to believe, and the two columns measure different things

concurrency.method: aggregate throughput against offered concurrency. The lowest level reaching PLATEAU_FRACTION of peak is the SATURATION POINT, which is a property of this host under this load — not a slot count, and not comparable across token budgets

identity_refusals.concurrency: `max_num_seqs` — the scheduler's batch width, which is what this field means — is not on vLLM 0.26.0's HTTP surface. Searched exhaustively on 2026-08-18: every parameterless GET in the server's own /openapi.json route table (11 answered) on srv1 and srv2, including /server_info's full engine config, all 122 /metrics series, and /v1/models. `vllm:cache_config_info.kv_cache_max_concurrency` looks like the answer and is NOT: it is KV-cache capacity, and it moves opposite to the flag — srv1 ran --max-num-seqs 8 and reported 16.004, srv2 ran 16 and reported 5.314. It is not unknowable, only unaskable: a concurrency ramp recovers it, and on srv1 it read the knee at exactly 8 — throughput plateauing at 106.5 tok/s and per-request latency flat at ~9.5s through n=8 before the queue forms. That is a measurement this capture must not make, because it would perturb the run it describes. The raw metrics are under native

weights.method: sha256 over every tensor's bytes in sorted key order across all shards, computed on the serving host: this engine states no weights digest on any endpoint

serving_config.note: two digests because one would move when somebody enabled a counter; the semantic half is the one a guard could key on. Nothing reads either for comparison (ADR-0027 D7)

readings.note: both plateaus are reported because their disagreement is readable: on a wide server they differ by design, since a larger batch is slower per request before any queueing starts. NEITHER is a slot count: an engine configured one slot returned a throughput plateau several times that. Computed on the levels that fully succeeded — see levels_used and levels_dropped. The former `batches` boolean is retired (D1): it claimed to say which column to believe, and the two columns measure different things

concurrency.method: aggregate throughput against offered concurrency. The lowest level reaching PLATEAU_FRACTION of peak is the SATURATION POINT, which is a property of this host under this load — not a slot count, and not comparable across token budgets

refusal.prose: Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-AWQ on srv2: the declaration does not fit this card. weights 9,518 MiB + declared KV 3,072 MiB + 733 MiB the process holds besides them = 13,323 MiB, and the card has 12,271 MiB free. Short by 1,052 MiB. 2,020 MiB is 10,773 KV tokens at this model's 196,608 B/token, which is either max_num_seqs 5 at the declared max_model_len 2,048, or max_model_len 1,346 at the declared max_num_seqs 8. This picks neither: which one to give up is the entry's decision, and a launcher that quietly chose would have the run measure a configuration nobody declared (ADR-0039 rule 2, #354). Nothing was measured.
